evidence_problems.detail: Element 1 of MINSEQE (reading-pack/08 s2) asks only for 'A description of the biological system, the samples, and the experimental variables being studied'. It does not require RIN, library preparation, sex, age, clone or passage columns, so the claim that the sheet 'lacks the sample attributes ... that MINSEQE element 1 requires' goes beyond what the quote says. The finding also treats study/samplesheet.csv as the 2.1 'laboratory spreadsheet' that 6.4 plans to deposit. Nothing in the DMP links the two. The sheet's own columns follow the nf-core/rnaseq input format, as TRE-6 notes, and it has no RNA-quality or library columns even though 2.1 says the lab spreadsheet records them. That suggests it may be a different file.

The finding admits that the plan gives no Calder sample size or description of the combined cohort. It still concludes that 'Six carriers cannot support any genetic association analysis of modifiers' and that the WGS design 'does not support' the analysis. DMP 6.3 describes a joint analysis with Calder, so six carriers are a contribution, not the whole cohort. The evidence supports 'not described', not 'not supported'. The claims about the sample size and design that modifier studies need come entirely from professional knowledge.

report_distortions.detail: 'These attributes' points back to RIN, library preparation, sex, age, clone and passage. Neither STW-3 nor reading-pack/08 says that element 1 requires those specific fields. Element 1 asks for a description of the samples and experimental variables. The report states the requirement more strongly than the finding or its source.

conformity_flags.detail: The upgrade rests on BIO-3's volume arithmetic. TRE had already anticipated this problem in round 1, in its referral saying 60 GB 'looks far too low ... This affects the NSRE storage request and costing (TRE-7)'. The 'existing allocation is not an NSRE workspace' point was already in STW-8 in round 1. The new cost figures (about £975 to £1,875 for project storage) do not show a change in materiality. In effect the severity has been brought into line with STW-8, without independent new evidence.

Marked 'kept' with no change_reason or new_evidence. However, the headline issue changed from 'roughly 1.5 to 3 TB' to '1.3 to 2.5 TB of retained data', and a statement about pipeline scratch space was added. This is an unrecorded revision. It is the corrected figure that STW-8 and TRE-7 now use for costing.

The substance of the finding changed from identifier and vocabulary problems to missing sample attributes. The new_evidence repeats BIO-7's observation (no RIN, library, sex, age or passage columns) and does not add independent evidence. The only addition is the MINSEQE element 1 quote, which does not support the specific attributes (see evidence_problems). After the revision, STW-3 largely converges on BIO-7.

unmerged_duplicates.detail: Both say the participant information covers only use 'for this study' and does not tell participants about the Calder/US sharing, archive deposit or the 'future analyses' in the Summary. Both cite the same source, reading-pack/06 section 2. They are reported separately (3.4 major and 3.4 minor) with different severities, and the report does not cross-reference them.

Both address the same 6.3 transfer of VCFs and clinical data to Calder. Both require IGO approval of the transfer mechanism and both recommend NSRE collaborator accounts as the preferred fix. They appear as two separate major items under section 6.3.
STW-3's working relies on the same samplesheet defects as BIO-6 (MNT-008 'Ctrl' and MNT-005 'stranded'). STW-3 is merged with BIO-7, but the overlap with BIO-6 is not acknowledged.

weakest_finding.detail: This is a new round-2 finding with 'reasoning' basis. It rests entirely on professional knowledge that is not in the pack, and it cites no DMP text beyond the six-carrier count and the phrase 'joint analysis'. Its central claim, that the WGS design cannot support the analysis, contradicts its own admission that the size of the Calder cohort is unknown.
